constants_used.models.M-frontier.positional_encoding: none (NoPE MLA; KDA decay + short conv carry order)

label: Illustrative toy inputs chosen so every step can be checked by hand with a calculator. They are not real model weights, activations or logits. Frequencies, angles and YaRN values are computed from M-dense's real config.

frequencies.formula: θ_i = base^(-2i/d), i = 0 .. d/2 - 1; pair i holds dims (2i, 2i+1) and turns by m·θ_i at position m

wavelength_tokens.text: 2π / θ_i: tokens for one full turn
2π / θ_i: tokens for one full turn
2π / θ_i: tokens for one full turn
2π / θ_i: tokens for one full turn
2π / θ_i: tokens for one full turn

frequencies.observation: Pair 0 turns 1 radian per token (a full turn every 6.28 tokens); pair 63 turns 1.24e-06 radian per token (a full turn every 5,063,256 tokens). Fast pairs resolve nearby order, slow pairs resolve long distances.

theta_toy.note: toy step of 30° per position so cos and sin are familiar values (0.5, 0.8660)

toy_2d.rotation: rotate (x, y) by angle a: (x cos a - y sin a, x sin a + y cos a)
toy_2d.why: (R_m q)·(R_n k) = q·(R_m^T R_n k) = q·(R_(n-m) k): rotating both vectors by their own positions leaves only the angle difference (n - m)·θ in the score, so attention sees relative position. RoPE is applied to Q and K only, never to V.
toy_2d.source: research/notes/05-papers-architecture.md §2.A A3 [S3 Su et al., RoFormer]

full_head_check.note: all 64 pairs of M-dense's head, with and without YaRN: the score depends only on m - n (differences come from float64 rounding of large angles)

yarn.idea: Pairs that turn many times within the original 4,096-token context (high frequency) already handle long text and keep their frequency. Pairs that turn less than once (low frequency) would meet angles never seen in training, so their frequency is divided by s = 64 (position interpolation). Pairs in between blend the two.

correction_range.formula: dim(r) = d · ln( L / (r · 2π) ) / (2 · ln base): the pair index whose rotation count over the original context L equals r
correction_range.rounding_note: low is floored and high is ceiled: floor(23.60) = 23, ceil(30.02) = 31, the same values note 01 §2.3 derives

ramp.formula: ramp_i = clamp((i - low) / (high - low), 0, 1); θ'_i = θ_i / s · ramp_i + θ_i · (1 - ramp_i)

regions.note_01_wording: note 01 §2.3 says 'pairs 0–22 keep original frequencies, 23–31 blend, 31–63 are divided by 64'. Computed exactly: pair 23 has ramp 0 (original) and pair 31 has ramp 1 (interpolated), so the strictly blended pairs are 24–30; 23 and 31 are the ends of the ramp.

rotation_check.text: Pair 23 turns 4.549 times in 4096 tokens (> beta_fast = 4); pair 31 turns 0.809 times (< beta_slow = 1). The index cut-offs agree with the paper's rotation-count rule here.

attention_factor.formula: attention_factor = 0.1 · ln(s) + 1 (HF: used when mscale_all_dim is 0)
attention_factor.effect: cos and sin tables are multiplied by 1.41589, so both q and k are scaled and every q·k score is multiplied by 1.41589^2 = 2.0047. In the paper's notation softmax(q·k / (t·sqrt(d))) with sqrt(1/t) = 0.1 ln(s) + 1, so 1/t = 2.0047.
attention_factor.history: Mistral's original config had mscale_all_dim 1.0, which made the factor get_mscale(64,1)/get_mscale(64,1) = 1.0; they set it to 0 because it 'caused long-context performance degradation'.

sources: research/notes/05-papers-architecture.md §2.A A4 [S4 Peng et al., YaRN eqs. 10-15]

nope_contrast.positional_encoding: none (NoPE MLA; KDA decay + short conv carry order)
nope_contrast.note: M-frontier (Kimi K3) has no positional encoding: its MLA layers are NoPE (no rotation; the 64 'rope' dims are not rotated) and its KDA layers carry order through their decay and short convolution. The report says it extends to 1M tokens without a RoPE base change or YaRN.
nope_contrast.note_source: research/notes/01b-kimi-k3.md §1 item 2 and §2.4 (NoPE MLA; KDA decay and short convolution carry order)
